findings.reason: as written the plan asserts a wiring that is not there, so it omits the required threading of the observed set through `PaneRowPath` into `RowPolicy`, and a literal implementer would search for a pass to extend and find none (the live follower at `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1235` and `follower_row_path` both stop short of the policy).
findings.text: the deliverable states `follower_row_path` "already receives the observed sessions; it passes them to `RowPolicy`, which exempts an observed session's rows from the observer-context hold", but `follower_row_path` (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:903-931`) passes the observed set only to its `selects` callable (`_follow_selects`), and neither `PaneRowPath.__init__` (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1528`) nor `RowPolicy.__init__` (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1109`) takes an observed argument — `RowPolicy`'s sole exemption is `_is_own_start` (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1163`), keyed on `own_session` and `kind == START_KIND`.

findings.reason: either the plan must state that `tests/test_follow_sweep_cadence.py` is re-anchored to carry a `from_state` (the change that actually delivers those ids), or the thirteen-id done-when cannot be met by the mechanism the deliverable describes.
findings.text: the deliverable says "The other family tests feed production-shaped rows: coordinator kinds or own-session starts, each with a session and a `from_state`", but the cadence tests the same section assigns as write paths (`tests/test_follow_sweep_cadence.py:45-54`) emit `event: "transition"` lines with no `from_state` (kind `(None, to_state)`), and §15's own Why and the cited report both call them "truncated rows with no `from_state`"; the stated mechanism (the observed-session exemption plus the own-session start exemption) therefore cannot make those ids pass, and the plan never says the cadence fixture is re-anchored.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/ticker.py`, `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py`, all eight named test files, the cited report, and commits `089cd7741` and its parent `6d28c3f50` all resolve; the self-link to `/reckon/plans/the-suite-is-green-at-head` is the plan itself.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the thirteen ids passing alone, the two pin files (`test_follow_settled_rows.py`, `test_row_policy_holds_observer_context.py`) staying green, and the no-added-failure population over the ticker/follow-commands importers are all measurable, and a negative control is named (drop the observed-session delivery; the observed-session cases must then fail).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the Why cites the follower-family report at a durable reports path (`.../reports/reckon/the-suite-is-green-at-head/follower-family-shared-cause/report.md`) and the gate is logged under the run directory, neither a scratchpad nor a node-local temp path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §15 names files, symbols and commits by what they are; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, path or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: two findings — the mechanism is described as running through a caller chain that does not exist, and the section's stated mechanism cannot deliver the cadence ids it must make pass.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable, repair the follower family's shared cause, with the cadence re-anchor serving that same goal rather than a second one.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §15 declares no depends-on/gates/informs edges (this plan carries its ordering in prose, every `data-links` is empty), and the relationship it relies on — §3 delegating the follower family to a single shared-cause node and requiring those ids to pass alone (§3, line 94) — is stated in the plan's own text and evidenced by the follower-family report.
